note: archon request-authentication and key-enrollment conformance vectors (docs/request.md), version 1, fixed by ADR 0010's status note of 4 October 2026 when §8's gate was met: a change to any byte here is a new wire version. It carries the request profile (§3–§5, §7 steps 1–7: the client's signature base, headers and signature, and every acceptance and refusal of the verifier short of replay, which is the server's) and key enrollment (§6: the binding, the new key's proof, and its verification in the SDK's possession scheme, domain archon-enroll/1). Purposes are given as hex so that a non-UTF-8 purpose can be a case; a lane decodes them before calling the scheme. Audience is a UTF-8 string. Entropy (nonce, transaction id, keys) is a case INPUT — the scheme never sources it. Signatures derived with OpenSSL 3.2.4, outside all three cores (vectors/tools/request-vectors.py).

enroll_binding.note: the pinned layout: version 0x01 ‖ u16 len ‖ purpose ‖ u16 len ‖ audience ‖ u16 len ‖ transaction ‖ new_key[32] ‖ intent_digest[32] (docs/request.md §6; fixed, ADR 0010's status note of 4 October 2026). Inputs {audience (utf-8 string), request{nonce, transaction, purpose (hex), new_key, intent_digest}}; expected {"ok": hex} or {"error": true}. The nonce is not part of the binding. Oversize audience refusals (a binding over the possession scheme's u16 field) are per-lane unit tests, not 64 KB vectors.
enroll_binding.name: basic

enroll_binding.note: the purpose is UTF-8 bytes, bound as given (no normalisation).
enroll_binding.name: unicode-purpose

enroll_binding.note: a one-byte transaction id is the minimum; it is opaque bytes.
enroll_binding.name: transaction-min

enroll_binding.note: 255 bytes is the transaction id's maximum.
enroll_binding.name: transaction-255

enroll_binding.note: an empty purpose is refused: the purpose is what separates an addition from a rotation or a recovery.
enroll_binding.name: purpose-empty-rejected

enroll_binding.note: a control character (U+0007) in the purpose is refused.
enroll_binding.name: purpose-control-rejected

enroll_binding.note: U+007F in the purpose is refused.
enroll_binding.name: purpose-del-rejected

enroll_binding.note: a purpose that is not valid UTF-8 (0xff) is refused.
enroll_binding.name: purpose-not-utf8-rejected

enroll_binding.note: an empty transaction id is refused: completion names a pending record.
enroll_binding.name: transaction-empty-rejected

enroll_binding.note: a control character in the audience is refused.
enroll_binding.name: audience-control-rejected

enroll_binding.note: the new key must be exactly 32 bytes.
enroll_binding.name: new-key-short-rejected

enroll_binding.note: the new key must be exactly 32 bytes.
enroll_binding.name: new-key-long-rejected

enroll_binding.note: the intent digest must be exactly 32 bytes.
enroll_binding.name: intent-digest-short-rejected

enroll_binding.note: the intent digest must be exactly 32 bytes.
enroll_binding.name: intent-digest-long-rejected

enroll_prove.note: the enrollment proof: possession by the NEW key in domain archon-enroll/1 over the server's nonce and the enrollment binding — Ed25519ph, context-string archon-enroll/1, over 0x01 ‖ u16 len ‖ nonce ‖ u16 len ‖ binding. Inputs {seed, audience, request}; expected {"ok": 128 hex} or {"error": true}. Signatures derived with OpenSSL 3.2.4 — an implementation outside all three cores.
enroll_prove.name: basic

enroll_prove.note: another purpose is another statement, and another signature.
enroll_prove.name: rotate-purpose

enroll_prove.note: a seed whose public key is not the request's new key is refused: only the key being enrolled proves.
enroll_prove.name: not-the-new-key-rejected

enroll_prove.note: a 15-byte nonce is refused by the possession scheme.
enroll_prove.name: nonce-short-rejected

enroll_prove.note: every binding refusal is a prove refusal: an empty audience.
enroll_prove.name: audience-empty-rejected

enroll_verify.note: verify the enrollment proof under the request's own new key: inputs {audience, request, sig}; expected {valid: bool}. Total: every shape failure is false. The substitutions are the content — each bound field must bind, and no signature of another shape is a proof.
enroll_verify.name: basic

enroll_verify.note: the same proof at another audience is not a proof there.
enroll_verify.name: wrong-audience

enroll_verify.note: the audience is bound byte for byte.
enroll_verify.name: audience-trailing-slash

enroll_verify.note: an addition's proof is not a rotation's.
enroll_verify.name: wrong-purpose

enroll_verify.note: the request names another new key, so the proof is checked under that key and fails.
enroll_verify.name: other-new-key

enroll_verify.note: the same bytes proved in archon-login/1 are not an enrollment proof.
enroll_verify.name: login-domain

enroll_verify.note: a plain Ed25519 signature over the possession message is not a proof.
enroll_verify.name: raw-signature

enroll_verify.note: Ed25519ph without the context is not a proof.
enroll_verify.name: ph-without-context

enroll_verify.note: a signature over the nonce alone is not a proof.
enroll_verify.name: bare-nonce

enroll_verify.note: a signature over the binding without the possession layout is not a proof.
enroll_verify.name: binding-without-possession-layout

enroll_verify.note: the new key's proof over a version-2 binding (0x02, every other byte the same) is not a version-1 proof: a verifier accepts only the version it implements (ADR 0010 §8).
enroll_verify.name: version-other

enroll_verify.note: a 15-byte nonce is false, not an error.
enroll_verify.name: nonce-short

enroll_verify.note: a control character in the request is false, not an error.
enroll_verify.name: purpose-control

enroll_verify.note: a 31-byte new key is false, not an error.
enroll_verify.name: new-key-short

request_sign.note: the client (docs/request.md §3–§4): inputs {seed, method, audience, request_target, body (hex), content_type (string or null), declared [[name, value]] in the product's order, created, expires, nonce (hex)}; expected {"ok": {base, headers}} — the RFC 9421 signature base as text, and the four headers archon adds, named in lowercase — or {"error": true}. Every signature is Ed25519ph in context archon-request/1 over the base, derived with OpenSSL 3.2.4 outside the cores. Fixed (ADR 0010, status note of 4 October 2026).
request_sign.name: basic

request_sign.note: a GET with no body and no Content-Type: the digest is the empty string's, and content-type is not covered.
request_sign.name: empty-body-get

request_sign.note: product-declared headers are covered in the product's order, after content-type.
request_sign.name: declared-headers

request_sign.name: audience-with-port

request_sign.note: an audience with no path: the origin is the audience.
request_sign.name: audience-at-origin

request_sign.name: method-case-kept

request_sign.name: method-space-rejected

request_sign.note: absolute form is not origin form.

request_verify.note: the verifier (docs/request.md §3.1, §5, §7 steps 1–7; replay is the server's): inputs {policy {audience, declared, max_lifetime, skew}, now, request {method, request_target, headers [[name, value]] as received, body (hex)}}; expected {"ok": {principal, created, expires, nonce (hex), target_uri}} or {"error": true}. Each refusal below breaks exactly one rule; where the case can be signed correctly it is, so the refusal comes from that rule and not from a bad signature. Fixed (ADR 0010, status note of 4 October 2026).
request_verify.name: basic

request_verify.note: header names are matched without regard to case.
request_verify.name: header-names-any-case

request_verify.note: a header named with U+212A KELVIN SIGN is not idempotency-key: names fold ASCII case only, so this is an unrelated header and not a second covered field.
request_verify.name: names-fold-ascii-only

request_verify.note: the Host and X-Forwarded-Host the request carries change nothing: @target-uri comes from the configured audience.
request_verify.name: host-is-not-authoritative

request_verify.note: a GET with no body and no Content-Type.
request_verify.name: empty-body-get

request_verify.note: a declared header the request does not carry is not covered.
request_verify.name: declared-absent-uncovered

request_verify.note: now = created − skew is the earliest acceptable time.
request_verify.name: fresh-at-earliest

request_verify.note: now = expires + skew − 1 is the latest acceptable time.
request_verify.name: fresh-at-latest

request_verify.note: expires − created = max_lifetime is accepted.
request_verify.name: lifetime-at-max
